moments.explanation: The brief makes the mission testable through role, objective, context, limits and done. The Mission Brief is the bounded contract for scope and acceptance.
key_points: An objective without boundaries invites improvisation.
Done criteria allow acceptance or rejection.
moments.application: Complete the five brief elements.
moments.check_question: Could someone outside the case tell what to approve?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, replace one vague verb with observable evidence.
moments.takeaway: The mission brief is the pilot's operating contract.
moments.handoff: Complete it with sufficient sources.

moments.explanation: A mission needs identified sources and an explicit statement of what is missing. Use only personal or authorized sources.
key_points: Broader access does not fix a missing source.
A material gap must stop or escalate.
moments.application: List sources and gaps separately.
moments.check_question: Which missing fact would change the plan or verdict?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, mark each source available, limited or absent.
moments.takeaway: Honesty about gaps protects the decision.
moments.handoff: Use the inventory to restrict tools and instructions.

moments.explanation: Instructions must state allowed steps, tools, prohibitions, escalation and done.
key_points: A tool never authorizes every possible use.
Every prohibition needs a safe response.
moments.application: Turn one prohibition into a stop condition.
moments.check_question: Does the agent know what to do when it cannot proceed?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, add “stop and request review” to one exception.
moments.takeaway: Useful limits state both what not to do and how to respond.
moments.handoff: Send the contract to the plan gate.

moments.explanation: Before execution, review sequence, sources, risk, gates and reversibility of the proposed plan. You compare the plan with your boundaries before approval.
key_points: The plan is a proposal subject to approval.
A missing source or permission blocks the affected step.
moments.application: Audit the plan before authorizing it.
moments.check_question: Is every action backed by a source and permission?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, mark one step to approve and one to correct.
moments.takeaway: Approving the objective does not replace approving the plan.
moments.handoff: Reduce the plan to a small, recoverable mission.

moments.explanation: The first pilot should be small, frequent, observable and recoverable if it fails. In this pilot, you do not send, publish, pay or change external systems.
key_points: Start without publishing, paying or sending.
Test the path and evidence first.
moments.application: Choose a controlled case and restoration path.
moments.check_question: Can you return to the prior state without relying on the agent?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, define a dry run and how you would restore state.
moments.takeaway: The first mission demonstrates control, not scale.
moments.handoff: Record the pilot to decide continuity.

moments.explanation: The pilot earns value through an informed keep, adjust or retire decision. Your verdict chooses keep, adjust or retire.
key_points: Compare evidence with done.
Version changes and retain exceptions.
moments.application: Close with a verdict and next gate.
moments.check_question: What evidence supports continuation, and what requires stopping?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic personal example, write a decision with reason, adjustment and review date.
moments.takeaway: Continuity is earned through evidence, not enthusiasm.
moments.handoff: Transfer the verdict to the playbook and next mission.

orientation.title: Personal pilot, visible control
orientation.body: Complete the workbook with an individual mission that has no external effect. Every step leaves a decision and evidence you can review. In this pilot, any execution happens outside the workbook and requires separate authorization.
orientation.use_case: Organize private notes into a weekly draft without sending or publishing it.
orientation.ready_when: You have a repeatable case, its sources and time to review every output.

preparation_prompts.title: Filter the case
preparation_prompts.prompt: List three repeatable cases. Assess frequency, stability, failure impact, observability and reversibility. Recommend one and explain why the others should wait.

preparation_prompts.title: Inventory evidence
preparation_prompts.purpose: Know which sources may be used and what is missing.
preparation_prompts.prompt: List inputs, sources, rights, definition of done and gaps. Mark the gap that requires stopping or asking.

preparation_prompts.title: Bound authority
preparation_prompts.purpose: Separate reading, proposing, approving and acting.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Classify each datum, tool and action as allowed, approval required or prohibited. Add owner, reviewer and escalation.

routes.title: Prepare
routes.brief: Choose a reversible case, set accountability and limit permissions.

steps.title: Choose a reversible case
steps.brief: Compare three processes and choose one that supports learning without exposing a sensitive decision.
actions: Describe each case's input and result.
Assess stability, failure impact and recovery.
Write the boundary you do not delegate.
steps.example: Synthetic example: prepare a weekly draft from private notes.
criteria: The case is repeatable and observable.
Your decision boundary is explicit.
steps.watch_out: Choose for control, not novelty.
steps.reflection: What makes this case appropriate for a first pilot?
steps.next_connection: The selected case moves to accountability, result and Definition of Done.

steps.title: Set accountability and result
steps.brief: Name who decides, who reviews and which output may be accepted.
actions: Write the result in observable terms.
State who retains your final approval.
steps.example: Synthetic example: you accept or reject the draft before using it.
criteria: One human decision is unambiguous.
Final approval remains with you.
steps.watch_out: The agent cannot be owner or approver.
steps.reflection: Who answers if the output looks right but breaks the contract?
steps.next_connection: The card supports classification of data, tools and actions.

steps.title: Design permissions and escalation
steps.brief: Grant only the required capability and define what happens at a boundary.
actions: Mark the permission you can revoke.
steps.example: Synthetic example: may read chosen notes and draft; may not send or delete.
criteria: Every action has explicit permission.
You can withdraw every granted permission.
steps.watch_out: Technical access is not authorization.
steps.reflection: Which permission can you remove without losing the useful draft?
steps.next_connection: The matrix feeds the mission brief.

routes.title: Pilot
routes.brief: Turn the case into a contract, approve the plan and observe a controlled run.

steps.title: Write the mission brief
steps.brief: Combine objective, context, sources, restrictions and done into one short contract.
actions: Bound the Mission Brief to one output.
steps.example: Synthetic example: produce a cited weekly draft from authorized notes.
criteria: The brief makes the output testable.
The output has a Definition of Done.
steps.watch_out: Avoid vague verbs such as “manage” or “solve.”
steps.reflection: Which phrase could be read as undeclared authority?
steps.next_connection: The brief becomes a plan subject to approval.

steps.title: Review the plan before execution
steps.brief: Require a sequence that respects sources, permissions, gates and recovery.
actions: Link every step to source and permission.
Reject one step outside your contract.
steps.example: Synthetic example: approve reading and drafting; reject publishing.
criteria: Every step fits the brief.
Every step respects your contract.
steps.watch_out: An approved objective does not authorize a defective plan.
steps.reflection: Which step would you change before allowing the test?
steps.next_connection: Only an approved plan enters the controlled case.

steps.title: Run and record the pilot
steps.brief: Process one controlled case and retain enough evidence to reconstruct decisions and exceptions.
actions: Log decisions, proposed actions and gates.
steps.example: Synthetic example: keep notes, draft and your verdict; do not send it.
criteria: The log connects input, decision and result.
The run leaves a reviewable record.
steps.watch_out: A fluent output does not prove compliance.
steps.reflection: Could you explain why each step was accepted or rejected?
steps.next_connection: The log is compared with the definition of done.

routes.title: Transfer
routes.brief: Compare evidence, decide continuity and revalidate before another context.

steps.title: Compare against done
steps.brief: Assess compliance, deviations and evidence without rewarding appearance or speed alone.
steps.example: Synthetic example: the draft cites every note but mixes two dates; adjust.
criteria: Every verdict points to evidence.
Your verdict cites case evidence.
steps.watch_out: Do not replace criteria with a general impression.
steps.reflection: Which deviation materially changes the decision?
steps.next_connection: Deviations move to recovery and correction.

steps.title: Decide keep, adjust or stop
steps.brief: Close the pilot with a verdict, corrections and accountability.
actions: Choose one correction under your control.
steps.example: Synthetic example: adjust the brief and repeat at the same scope.
criteria: The decision relies on pilot evidence.
The correction fits the next test.
steps.watch_out: Do not widen scope to rescue a failed pilot.
steps.reflection: What evidence would change your verdict?
steps.next_connection: Only a keep decision opens design of the next case.

steps.title: Transfer without scope creep
steps.brief: Reuse the learning and keep the same gates until the new context produces its own evidence.
actions: State what changes in the next case.
Test the package without expanding scope.
steps.example: Synthetic example: reuse the format for another folder after reviewing sources again.
criteria: Reused rules and new assumptions are distinct.
The new case keeps your boundaries.
steps.watch_out: A passed pilot does not certify every case.
steps.reflection: Which part of the contract becomes invalid when context changes?
steps.next_connection: The package feeds the next Masterclass or another bounded pilot.

rubric.label: Incomplete
rubric.description: Owner, sources, limits, gate or evidence are missing.

rubric.label: Controlled
rubric.description: The case is bounded and evidenced but needs one correction before repetition.

rubric.label: Transferable
rubric.description: Contract, execution, exceptions and verdict can be reviewed and adapted without widening authority.

transfer_challenge.title: Transfer challenge: one mission, one decision
transfer_challenge.brief: Apply the package to a new case and hold scope until its own evidence supports a decision.
actions: State what stays and what changes.
Close with keep, adjust or stop.
transfer_challenge.evidence: Versioned brief, approved plan, case log and verdict.
transfer_challenge.review_after: Review after one complete case; do not widen scope by calendar.

chapters.principle: Start where failure is visible and recoverable.
chapters.explanation: A stable case tests the contract without mixing novelty, sensitive authority and hidden dependencies.
chapters.decision: Choose or reject the case before designing autonomy.
actions: Reject external effects and high sensitivity.
chapters.rule: If you cannot observe and recover, it is not the first pilot.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: draft from private notes, without sending.
chapters.antipattern: Choosing the most complex process to signal ambition.
chapters.expected_evidence: Suitability matrix and rejection reasons.
chapters.limit: Suitability applies only to the assessed case and scope.

chapters.principle: Human accountability must be nameable.
chapters.explanation: The agent produces or proposes; a person answers for the objective and a separate review may test the result.
chapters.decision: Assign decision, review and acceptance before the brief.
chapters.rule: No agent is owner, approver or source of authority.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: you accept the draft and record why.
chapters.antipattern: Using “the team” as owner without a name or gate.
chapters.expected_evidence: Accountability card and verdicts.
chapters.limit: Human review cannot repair a vague contract by itself.

chapters.principle: Use only sufficient, traceable context.
chapters.explanation: Authorized sources support the plan; material gaps are declared and block the affected step.
chapters.decision: Authorize, limit or exclude every source.
chapters.rule: An inference never replaces a required source.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: use selected notes and mark the missing week.
chapters.antipattern: Granting broad access “just in case.”
chapters.expected_evidence: Source package, limits and gaps.
chapters.limit: More context may increase exposure without improving relevance.

chapters.principle: Authorize capabilities separately and by least privilege.
chapters.explanation: Reading, classifying, drafting and acting are distinct permissions with separate justification and revocation.
chapters.decision: Grant only what a testable draft requires.
chapters.rule: Anything undeclared remains prohibited.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: read notes and draft; never send or delete.
chapters.antipattern: Confusing available access with granted authority.
chapters.expected_evidence: Permission matrix and approval log.
chapters.limit: Least privilege limits impact; it does not remove review.

chapters.principle: Every boundary needs an operational response.
chapters.explanation: Prohibitions, missing data and ambiguity must lead to stop, escalation or clarification, never improvised authority.
chapters.decision: Define which condition triggers each response.
actions: Define how you will ask for help.
chapters.rule: When authority is insufficient, stop before acting.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: omit an unauthorized note and ask.
chapters.antipattern: Writing “be careful” without testable conduct.
chapters.expected_evidence: Condition-response table and exceptions.
chapters.limit: Escalation must not become automatic approval.

chapters.principle: Review the plan before any effect.
chapters.explanation: The gate corrects sequence, sources, permissions and reversibility while no environment has changed.
chapters.decision: Approve, correct or reject with explicit criteria.
chapters.rule: An approved objective does not authorize every plan.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: approve local drafting; reject publishing.
chapters.antipattern: Reviewing only after the action occurred.
chapters.expected_evidence: Versioned plan and gate verdict.
chapters.limit: An approved plan remains subject to exception and stop.

chapters.principle: A useful run can be reconstructed.
chapters.explanation: Input, version, decisions, actions, gates, exceptions and result form the minimum reviewable record.
chapters.decision: Accept output only with sufficient traceability.
chapters.rule: Fluency is not evidence of compliance.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: notes, draft, changes and personal verdict.
chapters.antipattern: Saving only the final output.
chapters.expected_evidence: Execution log and compliance table.
chapters.limit: The log explains the case; it does not predict future performance.

chapters.principle: Design the exception before it occurs.
chapters.explanation: A safe response states how to stop, who reviews and how to discard output or restore state.
chapters.decision: Stop, escalate or recover according to the stated condition.
chapters.rule: Never invent permission to resolve an exception.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: discard a draft that uses an excluded source.
chapters.antipattern: Continuing to “finish” after traceability is lost.
chapters.expected_evidence: Exception, decision and recovery log.
chapters.limit: Recovery does not remove the need to analyze cause.

chapters.principle: Continuity is a decision, not momentum.
chapters.explanation: Keep, adjust or retire depends on contract compliance, exceptions and changes required by another context.
chapters.decision: Issue a verdict and retain its evidence.
chapters.rule: Do not widen scope or permission to rescue a failed pilot.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: repeat the same case after fixing sources.
chapters.antipattern: Turning one good case into general authorization.
chapters.expected_evidence: Continuity decision and versioned package.
chapters.limit: A pass confirms that contract in that case, not every use.

glossary.definition: A bounded objective with context, restrictions and done.
A point where a person approves, corrects or stops.
Only the access or action required for the case.
A condition outside the expected flow that requires stop or escalation.
A documented return to a safe state or disposal of the output.

faq.question: May an agent approve its own plan?
faq.answer: No. The plan is a proposal; approval belongs to the accountable person named in the contract.

faq.question: What if a source is missing?
faq.answer: Declare the gap and stop the affected step. Never replace missing evidence with an assumption.

faq.question: When should permissions expand?
faq.answer: Only for a concrete need, after risk review and new approval. A good pilot does not grant general authority.

faq.question: What does a passed pilot mean?
faq.answer: It met done and its limits in that case; it does not validate the system for every context.

closing_checklist: Case, boundary, human owner and reviewer are written.
Sources, permissions and prohibitions are clear.
The plan was approved before the run.
Exceptions and recovery were recorded.
Continuity has a verdict, evidence and new authorization; this pilot grants no external effects.

graph_summary.title: From case to continuity
graph_summary.body: The prompts move from suitability to contract, permissions, plan, execution and verdict. None performs external actions. In this pilot, no prompt sends, publishes, pays or changes external systems.
graph_summary.independent_use: Use any prompt independently when you provide its declared input artifact; if it is missing, the prompt must ask or stop.

items.when: Before defining mission or permissions.
workflow: Recommend one and reject the others with reasons.

Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

The case keeps a personal boundary.

items.tradeoff: A simpler case teaches control before breadth.

items.when: After triage and before planning.
workflow: Document constraints, approval points and the Definition of Done.
guardrails: Add no implicit permissions.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.

Mission and Definition of Done are verifiable.
items.tradeoff: More precision limits flexibility but makes the pilot reviewable.

items.purpose: Prepare authorized sources and declare material gaps.
items.when: Before planning source-dependent steps.
workflow: Link each source to a need.
guardrails: Never fill gaps from memory or conjecture.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every source has use and limit.
Every source is within your right to use.

items.purpose: Define what the agent may read, propose or do.
items.when: After the brief and before instructions.
workflow: Classify allowed, approval required or prohibited.
guardrails: Available access is not authorization.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every capability maps to a step.
You can revoke every granted capability.

limits: Documents authority; it does not grant it. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Permission matrix: read the copy and propose labels = allowed; write a local preview = allowed; move or rename = approval required; delete, send, or publish = prohibited. Revocation: close the session and remove the copy.

items.purpose: Draft invariant instructions with limits and exception response.
items.when: Once mission, sources and permissions are defined.
workflow: Order the objective and allowed steps.
guardrails: Invent no tools, data or authority.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Allowed and prohibited conduct is testable.
Instructions preserve your final decision.

items.purpose: Decide whether the proposed plan fits the contract.
items.when: Before every run, including a pilot.
workflow: Trace steps to sources and permissions.
guardrails: An approved goal does not validate every step.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict per criterion.
Your verdict identifies the exact plan.
items.tradeoff: The gate adds review before effects instead of correction after effects. An approved verdict may support requesting a separate controlled run, but does not perform or authorize it by itself.
limits: The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.
items.demo_artifact: Case: organize authorized source notes for a weekly summary. Approved plan v1: verify the copy hash; classify 32 notes; save a preview; reconcile count and uncertainties; leave originals untouched. Recovery: delete the preview. Human approval is bound to this version and case.

execution_gate.action: Run the approved plan on an isolated copy outside NotebookLM. Do not send, publish, move, or delete originals. Record input, version, observed output, exceptions, decisions, and recovery.
execution_gate.criteria: Approval matches the executed version, at least one observed output exists, and the log confirms zero external effects. If the test was not run, do not proceed.

items.purpose: Reconstruct what happened and how exceptions were handled. It consumes the log from a separate controlled run; this prompt does not execute the plan.
items.when: After a controlled run or when reviewing a log.
guardrails: Never treat an absent record as success.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every decision has evidence.
The log comes from a separate controlled run.
edge_cases: Part of the log is missing.
The result looks right but broke a limit.

limits: Infers no cause or performance beyond evidence. Stop when data or authority is missing.

Synthetic observed output and execution log: 32 inputs read; 29 classified; 3 flagged as uncertain; preview stored locally; 0 originals changed; 0 messages sent or items published. Exception: one note looked like an instruction and was treated as content.
items.receive_override: Approved plan + observed output + execution log

items.purpose: Close the pilot with keep, adjust or stop.
items.when: After comparing the run with its contract.
workflow: Issue verdict, owner and next gate.
guardrails: Do not widen scope to compensate for failure.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: One decision with reason.
Continuity respects your original boundary.
edge_cases: The case passed but the next context changes permissions.
items.tradeoff: Repeating scope yields comparable evidence; widening adds coverage and uncertainty.
limits: Does not authorize a new context or external effect. Stop when data or authority is missing.

phases.label: Understand
phases.purpose: Distinguish assistance, delegation and orchestration without hiding accountability or coordination.

phases.label: Design
phases.purpose: Turn the case into a Mission Brief, with sources, permissions, human decision points (gates) and a Definition of Done.

phases.label: Pilot
phases.purpose: Approve, observe and review a reversible run before deciding continuity. In this pilot, no external effect is authorized.

moments.explanation: Delegation starts by turning known work into a bounded objective, not by asking the agent to “handle everything.” The sponsor sets the result and a separate reviewer accepts the output.
key_points: Name the intended result.
Make exclusions part of the contract.
moments.application: Define the result and one exclusion.
moments.check_question: Can you state what completes the mission and what does not belong to it?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write one sentence with objective, boundary and done condition.
moments.takeaway: Bound the mission before choosing what to delegate.
moments.handoff: Take the case to the suitability matrix.

moments.explanation: Doing a task faster is different from designing a repeatable, reviewable cycle.
key_points: Speed describes one run.
A system includes inputs, decisions and evidence.
moments.application: Draw the cycle that should repeat.
moments.check_question: Could the next run follow the same contract?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write input, decision, output and evidence.
moments.takeaway: Leverage requires an observable system, not a promise.
moments.handoff: Use the cycle to locate its bottleneck.

moments.explanation: The bottleneck may be a necessary human decision; removing it does not always improve the flow.
key_points: Separate avoidable waiting from essential judgment.
Keep approval where it protects the result.
moments.application: Mark where judgment is required.
moments.check_question: Which decision should the agent never assume?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, underline one point that needs human review.
moments.takeaway: Optimization does not mean erasing accountability.
moments.handoff: Compare that point with co-creation and delegation.

moments.explanation: Co-creation keeps step-by-step interaction; delegation assigns a bounded mission with agreed review. The team agrees cadence and review point.
key_points: Cadence and contract change.
Accountability does not move to the system.
moments.application: Classify the case as assistance or mission.
moments.check_question: Do you need dialogue at every step or review of a defined result?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, rewrite one task as an objective and keep one gate.
moments.takeaway: Delegation changes the workflow, not final accountability.
moments.handoff: Make the required coordination explicit.

moments.explanation: Agentic work still requires supervision, dependencies and exception handling. Every dependency has an accountable person or stop condition.
key_points: Coordination still has a cost.
Every dependency needs an owner or stop condition.
moments.application: Name one dependency and one exception.
moments.check_question: Who responds when an input is missing or a conflict appears?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, add an exception with a stop-or-escalate response.
moments.takeaway: Do not count shifted supervision as eliminated work.
moments.handoff: Move from the idea to the capabilities you will authorize.

moments.explanation: Context, memory, tools and actions are separate permissions, not one bundle. Data custody limits each permission.
key_points: Authorize only what the case needs.
Undeclared access remains prohibited.
moments.application: Separate reading, proposing and acting.
moments.check_question: What is the minimum permission needed for a reviewable draft?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, create three columns: may read, may propose, may not do.
moments.takeaway: Useful capability is specific and revocable.
moments.handoff: Connect permissions to the work cycle.

moments.explanation: A governed cycle defines input, decision, action, evidence and stop before execution.
key_points: Every step produces a reviewable signal.
The stop condition prevents momentum from becoming authority.
moments.application: Order the five parts of the cycle.
moments.check_question: What evidence allows the next step?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write one advance condition and one stop condition.
moments.takeaway: Without visible states, execution cannot be reviewed.
moments.handoff: Place human controls inside the cycle.

moments.explanation: Human gates sit before sensitive actions and when results require acceptance. The gate authority may approve, correct or stop.
key_points: Plan approval is not approval of every effect.
A reviewer needs criteria, not only an alert.
moments.application: Choose one gate before and one after.
moments.check_question: What must a person see to approve or reject?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write a verdict: approve, correct or stop.
moments.takeaway: Human control works when it has information and power to stop.
moments.handoff: Separate deliverable quality from system quality.

moments.explanation: Producing a strong deliverable and designing a sound system are related but distinct jobs.
key_points: The craft role protects the output.
The orchestration role protects rules, evidence and continuity.
moments.application: Assign one review to each role.
moments.check_question: What belongs to output review and what belongs to process review?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write one deliverable criterion and one system criterion.
moments.takeaway: Quality requires review of both result and mechanism.
moments.handoff: Turn both criteria into a mission brief.

moments.explanation: The brief makes the mission testable through role, objective, context, limits and done. The Mission Brief assigns scope, accountability and acceptance.
key_points: An objective without boundaries invites improvisation.
Done criteria allow acceptance or rejection.
moments.application: Complete the five brief elements.
moments.check_question: Could someone outside the case tell what to approve?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, replace one vague verb with observable evidence.
moments.takeaway: The mission brief is the pilot's operating contract.
moments.handoff: Complete it with sufficient sources.

moments.explanation: A mission needs identified sources and an explicit statement of what is missing. Provenance, rights and gaps accompany every source.
key_points: Broader access does not fix a missing source.
A material gap must stop or escalate.
moments.application: List sources and gaps separately.
moments.check_question: Which missing fact would change the plan or verdict?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, mark each source available, limited or absent.
moments.takeaway: Honesty about gaps protects the decision.
moments.handoff: Use the inventory to restrict tools and instructions.

moments.explanation: Instructions must state allowed steps, tools, prohibitions, escalation and done.
key_points: A tool never authorizes every possible use.
Every prohibition needs a safe response.
moments.application: Turn one prohibition into a stop condition.
moments.check_question: Does the agent know what to do when it cannot proceed?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, add “stop and request review” to one exception.
moments.takeaway: Useful limits state both what not to do and how to respond.
moments.handoff: Send the contract to the plan gate.

moments.explanation: Before execution, review sequence, sources, risk, gates and reversibility of the proposed plan. The reviewer compares plan, risk and reversibility.
key_points: The plan is a proposal subject to approval.
A missing source or permission blocks the affected step.
moments.application: Audit the plan before authorizing it.
moments.check_question: Is every action backed by a source and permission?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, mark one step to approve and one to correct.
moments.takeaway: Approving the objective does not replace approving the plan.
moments.handoff: Reduce the plan to a small, recoverable mission.

moments.explanation: The first pilot should be small, frequent, observable and recoverable if it fails. In this pilot, the team does not reply, publish, pay or change the source system.
key_points: Start without publishing, paying or sending.
Test the path and evidence first.
moments.application: Choose a controlled case and restoration path.
moments.check_question: Can you return to the prior state without relying on the agent?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, define a dry run and how you would restore state.
moments.takeaway: The first mission demonstrates control, not scale.
moments.handoff: Record the pilot to decide continuity.

moments.explanation: The pilot earns value through an informed keep, adjust or retire decision. The sponsor decides adoption only with evidence and visible exceptions.
key_points: Compare evidence with done.
Version changes and retain exceptions.
moments.application: Close with a verdict and next gate.
moments.check_question: What evidence supports continuation, and what requires stopping?
moments.micro_practice: In the synthetic team example, write a decision with reason, adjustment and review date.
moments.takeaway: Continuity is earned through evidence, not enthusiasm.
moments.handoff: Transfer the verdict to the playbook and next mission.

orientation.title: Team pilot, explicit authority
orientation.body: Complete the workbook with a bounded internal process. Every step assigns an owner, reviewer, permissions, dependencies and evidence. In this pilot, any execution happens outside the workbook and requires separate authorization.
orientation.use_case: Classify internal requests into a draft queue without replying or changing the source system.
orientation.ready_when: The owner accepts the case, a reviewer is named and permissions can be constrained.

preparation_prompts.title: Filter the case
preparation_prompts.prompt: List three repeatable cases. Assess frequency, stability, failure impact, observability and reversibility. Recommend one and explain why the others should wait.

preparation_prompts.title: Inventory evidence
preparation_prompts.purpose: Know which sources may be used and what is missing.
preparation_prompts.prompt: List inputs, sources, rights, definition of done and gaps. Mark the gap that requires stopping or asking.

preparation_prompts.title: Bound authority
preparation_prompts.purpose: Separate reading, proposing, approving and acting.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Classify each datum, tool and action as allowed, approval required or prohibited. Add owner, reviewer and escalation.

routes.title: Prepare
routes.brief: Choose a reversible case, set accountability and limit permissions.

steps.title: Choose a reversible case
steps.brief: Compare three processes and choose one that supports learning without exposing a sensitive decision.
actions: Describe each case's input and result.
Assess stability, failure impact and recovery.
Assign a case sponsor and recovery owner.
steps.example: Synthetic example: classify internal requests into a draft queue.
criteria: The case is repeatable and observable.
Sponsor and recovery have distinct accountability.
steps.watch_out: Choose for control, not novelty.
steps.reflection: What makes this case appropriate for a first pilot?
steps.next_connection: The selected case moves to accountability, result and Definition of Done.

steps.title: Set accountability and result
steps.brief: Name who decides, who reviews and which output may be accepted.
actions: Write the result in observable terms.
Name the output owner and separate reviewer.
steps.example: Synthetic example: the owner accepts classification and the reviewer checks a sample.
criteria: One human decision is unambiguous.
Output, acceptance and dependency have owners.
steps.watch_out: The agent cannot be owner or approver.
steps.reflection: Who answers if the output looks right but breaks the contract?
steps.next_connection: The card supports classification of data, tools and actions.

steps.title: Design permissions and escalation
steps.brief: Grant only the required capability and define what happens at a boundary.
actions: Link every permission to custody and revocation.
steps.example: Synthetic example: may read an authorized export and propose labels; may not write to the system.
criteria: Every action has explicit permission.
Custody and revocation are documented.
steps.watch_out: Technical access is not authorization.
steps.reflection: Which permission can you remove without losing the useful draft?
steps.next_connection: The matrix feeds the mission brief.

routes.title: Pilot
routes.brief: Turn the case into a contract, approve the plan and observe a controlled run.

steps.title: Write the mission brief
steps.brief: Combine objective, context, sources, restrictions and done into one short contract.
actions: Align the Mission Brief with acceptance and dependencies.
steps.example: Synthetic example: produce a draft queue with source and classification reason.
criteria: The brief makes the output testable.
The contract assigns acceptance and escalation.
steps.watch_out: Avoid vague verbs such as “manage” or “solve.”
steps.reflection: Which phrase could be read as undeclared authority?
steps.next_connection: The brief becomes a plan subject to approval.

steps.title: Review the plan before execution
steps.brief: Require a sequence that respects sources, permissions, gates and recovery.
actions: Link every step to source and permission.
Record who approves or returns each step.
steps.example: Synthetic example: approve sandbox classification; reject production writes.
criteria: Every step fits the brief.
Every verdict has defined authority.
steps.watch_out: An approved objective does not authorize a defective plan.
steps.reflection: Which step would you change before allowing the test?
steps.next_connection: Only an approved plan enters the controlled case.

steps.title: Run and record the pilot
steps.brief: Process one controlled case and retain enough evidence to reconstruct decisions and exceptions.
actions: Log decisions, proposed actions and gates.
Give the log to an independent reviewer.
steps.example: Synthetic example: keep batch, proposed labels, reviews and rejection; do not sync.
criteria: The log connects input, decision and result.
The log preserves version, gate and exception.
steps.watch_out: A fluent output does not prove compliance.
steps.reflection: Could you explain why each step was accepted or rejected?
steps.next_connection: The log is compared with the definition of done.

routes.title: Transfer
routes.brief: Compare evidence, decide continuity and revalidate before another context.

steps.title: Compare against done
steps.brief: Assess compliance, deviations and evidence without rewarding appearance or speed alone.
actions: Submit the result to the acceptance gate.
steps.example: Synthetic example: the queue retains sources but three cases lack reasons; it fails.
criteria: Every verdict points to evidence.
Acceptance and rejection use the same criteria.
steps.watch_out: Do not replace criteria with a general impression.
steps.reflection: Which deviation materially changes the decision?
steps.next_connection: Deviations move to recovery and correction.

steps.title: Decide keep, adjust or stop
steps.brief: Close the pilot with a verdict, corrections and accountability.
steps.example: Synthetic example: stop until source rights are clear and an owner is assigned.
criteria: The decision relies on pilot evidence.
Every correction has an owner and date.
steps.watch_out: Do not widen scope to rescue a failed pilot.
steps.reflection: What evidence would change your verdict?
steps.next_connection: Only a keep decision opens design of the next case.

steps.title: Transfer without scope creep
steps.brief: Reuse the learning and keep the same gates until the new context produces its own evidence.
actions: State what changes in the next case.
Approve adoption only after reviewing the new case.
steps.example: Synthetic example: test another category in sandbox while retaining owners and gates.
criteria: Reused rules and new assumptions are distinct.
Adoption preserves rights and a new gate.
steps.watch_out: A passed pilot does not certify every case.
steps.reflection: Which part of the contract becomes invalid when context changes?
steps.next_connection: The package feeds the next Masterclass or another bounded pilot.

rubric.label: Incomplete
rubric.description: The team has not yet assigned an owner, reviewer, permissions, sources or enough evidence to authorize the case.

rubric.label: Controlled
rubric.description: Owner and reviewer run a bounded case and retain evidence, but the team must correct one condition before repeating it.

rubric.label: Transferable
rubric.description: Another team can review and adapt the mission, permissions, exceptions and verdict without widening approved authority.

transfer_challenge.title: Transfer challenge: one governed mission
transfer_challenge.brief: Move the package to another team workflow without inheriting permissions or assumptions from the previous pilot.
actions: Assign an owner and reviewer for the new workflow.
Revalidate sources, permissions, dependencies and the approval point.
Record the adopt, adjust or retire verdict.
transfer_challenge.evidence: Versioned mission brief, permission matrix, approved plan, execution log and team verdict.
transfer_challenge.review_after: Review after one authorized case and before expanding to another team or system.

chapters.principle: Start where failure is visible and recoverable.
chapters.explanation: A stable case tests the contract without mixing novelty, sensitive authority and hidden dependencies.
chapters.decision: Choose or reject the case before designing autonomy.
actions: Reject external effects and high sensitivity.
chapters.rule: If you cannot observe and recover, it is not the first pilot.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: sandbox classification, without replying.
chapters.antipattern: Choosing the most complex process to signal ambition.
chapters.expected_evidence: Suitability matrix and rejection reasons.
chapters.limit: Suitability applies only to the assessed case and scope.

chapters.principle: Human accountability must be nameable.
chapters.explanation: The agent produces or proposes; a person answers for the objective and a separate review may test the result.
chapters.decision: Assign decision, review and acceptance before the brief.
chapters.rule: No agent is owner, approver or source of authority.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: Operations owns the decision; Quality reviews it.
chapters.antipattern: Using “the team” as owner without a name or gate.
chapters.expected_evidence: Accountability card and verdicts.
chapters.limit: Human review cannot repair a vague contract by itself.

chapters.principle: Use only sufficient, traceable context.
chapters.explanation: Authorized sources support the plan; material gaps are declared and block the affected step.
chapters.decision: Authorize, limit or exclude every source.
chapters.rule: An inference never replaces a required source.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: use an approved export and exclude attachments without rights.
chapters.antipattern: Granting broad access “just in case.”
chapters.expected_evidence: Source package, limits and gaps.
chapters.limit: More context may increase exposure without improving relevance.

chapters.principle: Authorize capabilities separately and by least privilege.
chapters.explanation: Reading, classifying, drafting and acting are distinct permissions with separate justification and revocation.
chapters.decision: Grant only what a testable draft requires.
chapters.rule: Anything undeclared remains prohibited.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: read export and propose labels; never write to the system.
chapters.antipattern: Confusing available access with granted authority.
chapters.expected_evidence: Permission matrix and approval log.
chapters.limit: Least privilege limits impact; it does not remove review.

chapters.principle: Every boundary needs an operational response.
chapters.explanation: Prohibitions, missing data and ambiguity must lead to stop, escalation or clarification, never improvised authority.
chapters.decision: Define which condition triggers each response.
chapters.rule: When authority is insufficient, stop before acting.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: escalate any request needing a reply; never send it.
chapters.antipattern: Writing “be careful” without testable conduct.
chapters.expected_evidence: Condition-response table and exceptions.
chapters.limit: Escalation must not become automatic approval.

chapters.principle: Review the plan before any effect.
chapters.explanation: The gate corrects sequence, sources, permissions and reversibility while no environment has changed.
chapters.decision: Approve, correct or reject with explicit criteria.
chapters.rule: An approved objective does not authorize every plan.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: approve sandbox; reject production writes.
chapters.antipattern: Reviewing only after the action occurred.
chapters.expected_evidence: Versioned plan and gate verdict.
chapters.limit: An approved plan remains subject to exception and stop.

chapters.principle: A useful run can be reconstructed.
chapters.explanation: Input, version, decisions, actions, gates, exceptions and result form the minimum reviewable record.
chapters.decision: Accept output only with sufficient traceability.
actions: Give the log to the compliance reviewer.
chapters.rule: Fluency is not evidence of compliance.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: batch, labels, approvals and reviewer rejection.
chapters.antipattern: Saving only the final output.
chapters.expected_evidence: Execution log and compliance table.
chapters.limit: The log explains the case; it does not predict future performance.

chapters.principle: Design the exception before it occurs.
chapters.explanation: A safe response states how to stop, who reviews and how to discard output or restore state.
chapters.decision: Stop, escalate or recover according to the stated condition.
chapters.rule: Never invent permission to resolve an exception.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: freeze the batch and restore the prior queue.
chapters.antipattern: Continuing to “finish” after traceability is lost.
chapters.expected_evidence: Exception, decision and recovery log.
chapters.limit: Recovery does not remove the need to analyze cause.

chapters.principle: Continuity is a decision, not momentum.
chapters.explanation: Keep, adjust or retire depends on contract compliance, exceptions and changes required by another context.
chapters.decision: Issue a verdict and retain its evidence.
chapters.rule: Do not widen scope or permission to rescue a failed pilot.
chapters.example: Synthetic example: stop until rights are clear and a dependency has an owner.
chapters.antipattern: Turning one good case into general authorization.
chapters.expected_evidence: Continuity decision and versioned package.
chapters.limit: A pass confirms that contract in that case, not every use.

glossary.definition: A bounded objective with context, restrictions and done.
A point where a person approves, corrects or stops.
Only the access or action required for the case.
A condition outside the expected flow that requires stop or escalation.
A documented return to a safe state or disposal of the output.

faq.question: May an agent approve its own plan?
faq.answer: No. The plan is a proposal; approval belongs to the accountable person named in the contract.

faq.question: What if a source is missing?
faq.answer: Declare the gap and stop the affected step. Never replace missing evidence with an assumption.

faq.question: When should permissions expand?
faq.answer: Only for a concrete need, after risk review and new approval. A good pilot does not grant general authority.

faq.question: What does a passed pilot mean?
faq.answer: It met done and its limits in that case; it does not validate the system for every context.

closing_checklist: Case, boundary, human owner and reviewer are written.
Sources, permissions and prohibitions are clear.
The plan was approved before the run.
Exceptions and recovery were recorded.
Continuity has a verdict, evidence and new authorization; this pilot grants no external effects.

graph_summary.title: From case to continuity
graph_summary.body: The prompts move from suitability to contract, permissions, plan, execution and verdict. None performs external actions. In this pilot, no prompt sends, publishes, pays or changes external systems.
graph_summary.independent_use: Use any prompt independently when you provide its declared input artifact; if it is missing, the prompt must ask or stop.

items.purpose: Select a small, observable and reversible case.
items.when: Before defining mission or permissions.
workflow: Recommend one and reject the others with reasons.
guardrails: Reject payments, publishing, sending and sensitive decisions.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict for every candidate.
Sponsor and recovery are assigned.
edge_cases: Impact depends on a missing source.
items.tradeoff: A simpler case teaches control before breadth.
limits: Does not authorize design or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Selection: classify 80 internal requests by type, urgency, and suggested team using a de-identified CSV. Rejected: ticket reassignment. Boundary: do not write to the service desk or notify anyone.

items.purpose: Turn the approved case into a bounded mission with a result, exclusions and a verifiable Definition of Done. Assign an output owner and acceptance reviewer.
items.when: After triage and before planning.
workflow: Document constraints, approval points and the Definition of Done.
guardrails: Add no implicit permissions.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Clear objective and exclusions.
Mission, acceptance and dependency have owners.
items.tradeoff: More precision limits flexibility but makes the pilot reviewable.
limits: The brief does not approve the plan or execution. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Approved Mission Brief: produce a classification preview for 80 internal requests. Output owner: operations lead; acceptance reviewer: service desk owner. Definition of Done: 80 rows with confidence and exceptions, with no production changes.

items.purpose: Prepare authorized sources and declare material gaps.
items.when: Before planning source-dependent steps.
workflow: Link each source to a need.
guardrails: Never fill gaps from memory or conjecture.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every source has use and limit.
Provenance, rights and gaps are recorded.
items.tradeoff: Fewer authorized sources may limit coverage while protecting traceability.
limits: Does not validate claims unsupported by the sources. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Authorized inventory: de-identified export of 80 requests, current taxonomy v3, and priority policy. Internal provenance and rights are recorded. Gap: the policy does not resolve requests that fit two teams.

items.purpose: Define what the agent may read, propose or do.
items.when: After the brief and before instructions.
workflow: Classify allowed, approval required or prohibited.
guardrails: Available access is not authorization.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every capability maps to a step.
Every permission has custody and revocation.
edge_cases: One tool combines read and write.
items.tradeoff: Narrow permissions require more gates but reduce unintended effects.
limits: Documents authority; it does not grant it. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Permission matrix: read CSV and policies = allowed; propose category, priority, and team = allowed; write an isolated preview = allowed; reassign, close, or notify = approval required and outside the pilot. Revocation: remove the file and temporary credential.

items.purpose: Draft invariant instructions with limits and exception response.
items.when: Once mission, sources and permissions are defined.
workflow: Order the objective and allowed steps.
guardrails: Invent no tools, data or authority.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Allowed and prohibited conduct is testable.
The exception has escalation authority.
edge_cases: The output requires a prohibited action.
items.tradeoff: Explicit rules reduce improvisation and may require more clarification.
limits: Produces an instruction draft; it does not activate an agent. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Instructions v1: apply taxonomy v3; cite the rule used; flag low confidence; do not infer identity; stop on sensitive data or conflicting rules; produce only a preview. The team retains the operational decision.

items.purpose: Decide whether the proposed plan fits the contract.
items.when: Before every run, including a pilot.
workflow: Trace steps to sources and permissions.
guardrails: An approved goal does not validate every step.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict per criterion.
The gate identifies version and reviewer.
items.tradeoff: The gate adds review before effects instead of correction after effects. An approved verdict may support requesting a separate controlled run, but does not perform or authorize it by itself.
limits: The verdict applies only to the reviewed version. Stop when data or authority is missing. The move to prompt-07 requires a log produced by a separate authorized run.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Approved plan v3: test a fixed 20-request sample; validate sources and permissions; produce a preview; review five cases; log exceptions. Recovery: remove the isolated output. Human review is bound to version v3 and sample S-20.

execution_gate.action: Run the approved plan on an isolated copy outside NotebookLM. Do not send, publish, move, or delete originals. Record input, version, observed output, exceptions, decisions, and recovery.
execution_gate.criteria: Approval matches the executed version, at least one observed output exists, and the log confirms zero external effects. If the test was not run, do not proceed.

items.purpose: Reconstruct what happened and how exceptions were handled. It consumes the log from a separate controlled run; this prompt does not execute the plan.
items.when: After a controlled run or when reviewing a log.
guardrails: Never treat an absent record as success.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every decision has evidence.
The external log preserves version, decisions and exceptions.
edge_cases: Part of the log is missing.
The result looks right but broke a limit.
items.tradeoff: Logging takes time and makes the case reviewable.
limits: Infers no cause or performance beyond evidence. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. Synthetic observed output and execution log: 20 requests processed; 17 clearly classified; 3 escalated for ambiguity; five reviewed by the service desk; 0 writes, reassignments, or notifications. A conflicting rule stopped case 14.
items.receive_override: Approved plan + observed output + execution log

items.purpose: Close the pilot with keep, adjust or stop.
items.when: After comparing the run with its contract.
workflow: Issue verdict, owner and next gate.
guardrails: Do not widen scope to compensate for failure.
Authorize no external effects and invent no evidence.
acceptance_criteria: One decision with reason.
Adoption has a sponsor and new gate.
edge_cases: The case passed but the next context changes permissions.
items.tradeoff: Repeating scope yields comparable evidence; widening adds coverage and uncertainty.
limits: Does not authorize a new context or external effect. Stop when data or authority is missing.
items.demo_artifact: Case: classify internal requests without sending responses. After Action Review: ADJUST. Clarify the dual-team rule and repeat the same sample before expanding. Evidence: 17/20 clear, 3 escalated, zero effects. Owner: operations lead; next gate: policy review.

phases.label: Compreender
phases.purpose: Distinguir assistência, delegação e orquestração sem esconder responsabilidade ou coordenação.

phases.label: Desenhar
phases.purpose: Transformar o caso em Mission Brief (brief de missão), com fontes, permissões, pontos de decisão humana (pontos de controle) e critério de conclusão (Definition of Done).

phases.label: Pilotar
phases.purpose: Aprovar, observar e revisar uma execução reversível antes de decidir continuidade. Neste piloto, nenhum efeito externo é autorizado.

moments.explanation: Delegar começa por transformar trabalho conhecido em objetivo delimitado; não por pedir «faça tudo». Seu caso preserva uma fronteira pessoal verificável.
key_points: O resultado deve ser nomeável.
O que fica fora também integra o contrato.
moments.application: Delimite o resultado e uma exclusão.
moments.check_question: Você consegue dizer o que encerra a missão e o que não pertence a ela?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, escreva uma frase com objetivo, fronteira e condição de concluído.
moments.takeaway: Primeiro delimite; depois decida o que delegar.
moments.handoff: Leve o caso à matriz de adequação.

moments.explanation: Fazer uma tarefa mais rápido é diferente de desenhar um ciclo repetível e revisável.
key_points: Velocidade descreve uma execução.
O sistema inclui entradas, decisões e evidência.
moments.application: Desenhe o ciclo que deve se repetir.
moments.check_question: A próxima execução poderia seguir o mesmo contrato?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, anote entrada, decisão, saída e evidência.
moments.takeaway: Alavancagem exige sistema observável, não promessa.
moments.handoff: Use o ciclo para localizar o gargalo.

moments.explanation: O gargalo pode estar em uma decisão humana necessária; removê-la nem sempre melhora o fluxo.
key_points: Separe espera evitável de critério indispensável.
Preserve uma aprovação quando ela protege o resultado.
moments.application: Marque onde seu critério intervém.
moments.check_question: Qual decisão o agente nunca deve assumir?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, sublinhe um ponto que exige revisão humana.
moments.takeaway: Otimizar não significa apagar responsabilidade.
moments.handoff: Compare esse ponto com cocriação e delegação.

moments.explanation: Cocriar mantém interação passo a passo; delegar entrega uma missão limitada com revisão acordada. Você escolhe quando conversar e quando revisar.
key_points: A cadência e o contrato mudam.
A responsabilidade não passa ao sistema.
moments.application: Classifique o caso como assistência ou missão.
moments.check_question: Você precisa conversar em cada passo ou revisar um resultado definido?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, reescreva uma tarefa como objetivo e preserve um ponto de controle.
moments.takeaway: Delegar muda o modo de trabalho, não a responsabilidade final.
moments.handoff: Explicite a coordenação que o novo modo exige.

moments.explanation: Um fluxo agêntico também requer supervisão, dependências e tratamento de exceções. Separe seus limites de qualquer dependência externa.
key_points: Coordenação continua tendo custo.
Cada dependência precisa de responsável ou condição de parada.
moments.application: Nomeie uma dependência e uma exceção.
moments.check_question: Quem responde quando falta uma entrada ou surge conflito?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, adicione uma exceção com resposta de parar ou escalar.
moments.takeaway: Não conte como economia o trabalho apenas transferido à supervisão.
moments.handoff: Passe da ideia às capacidades que serão autorizadas.

moments.explanation: Contexto, memória, ferramentas e ações são permissões distintas; não um pacote único. Autorize apenas seus próprios dados e ferramentas.
key_points: Autorize apenas o necessário para o caso.
Acesso não declarado permanece proibido.
moments.application: Separe ler, propor e agir.
moments.check_question: Qual é a permissão mínima para produzir um rascunho verificável?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, crie três colunas: pode ler, pode propor, não pode fazer.
moments.takeaway: Capacidade útil é específica e revogável.
moments.handoff: Conecte permissões ao ciclo de trabalho.

moments.explanation: Um ciclo governado define entrada, decisão, ação, evidência e parada antes de executar.
key_points: Cada passo produz um sinal revisável.
A condição de parada evita continuar por inércia.
moments.application: Ordene as cinco partes do ciclo.
moments.check_question: Que evidência permite avançar ao próximo passo?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, escreva uma condição de avanço e outra de parada.
moments.takeaway: Sem estados visíveis, a execução não pode ser revisada.
moments.handoff: Posicione controles humanos nesse ciclo.

moments.explanation: pontos de controle humanos ficam antes de ações sensíveis e na aceitação dos resultados. Sua aprovação preserva poder real de interromper.
key_points: Aprovar o plano não aprova qualquer efeito.
O revisor precisa de critérios, não apenas um alerta.
moments.application: Escolha um ponto de controle anterior e outro posterior.
moments.check_question: O que uma pessoa deve ver para aprovar ou rejeitar?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, redija um veredito: aprovar, corrigir ou parar.
moments.takeaway: Controle humano funciona quando há informação e poder de parada.
moments.handoff: Separe qualidade do entregável e do sistema.

moments.explanation: Produzir bem o entregável e desenhar bem o sistema são trabalhos relacionados, mas diferentes.
key_points: O artesão protege a saída.
O orquestrador protege regras, evidência e continuidade.
moments.application: Atribua uma revisão a cada papel.
moments.check_question: O que pertence à revisão da saída e o que pertence à revisão do processo?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, anote um critério do entregável e outro do sistema.
moments.takeaway: Qualidade exige revisar resultado e mecanismo.
moments.handoff: Converta os dois critérios em briefing de missão.

moments.explanation: O briefing torna a missão verificável ao fixar papel, objetivo, contexto, limites e critérios de conclusão. O Mission Brief —brief de missão— fixa escopo e critério de aceitação.
key_points: Objetivo sem fronteira convida à improvisação.
A definição de concluído permite aceitar ou rejeitar.
moments.application: Complete os cinco elementos do briefing.
moments.check_question: Alguém fora do caso saberia o que aprovar?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, troque um verbo vago por evidência observável.
moments.takeaway: O briefing é o contrato operacional do piloto.
moments.handoff: Complete o contrato com fontes suficientes.

moments.explanation: Uma missão precisa de fontes identificadas e de declaração explícita do que falta. Use somente fontes próprias ou autorizadas.
key_points: Mais acesso não corrige fonte ausente.
Uma lacuna material deve parar ou escalar.
moments.application: Liste fontes e lacunas separadamente.
moments.check_question: Qual dado ausente mudaria o plano ou o veredito?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, marque cada fonte como disponível, limitada ou ausente.
moments.takeaway: Honestidade sobre lacunas protege a decisão.
moments.handoff: Use o inventário para restringir ferramentas e instruções.

moments.explanation: As instruções devem declarar passos, ferramentas, proibições, escalonamento e condição de concluído.
key_points: Uma ferramenta não autoriza todo uso possível.
Toda proibição precisa de resposta segura.
moments.application: Transforme uma proibição em condição de parada.
moments.check_question: O agente sabe o que fazer quando não pode continuar?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, adicione «pare e peça revisão» a uma exceção.
moments.takeaway: Limites úteis dizem o que não fazer e como responder.
moments.handoff: Envie o contrato ao ponto de controle do plano.

moments.explanation: Antes de executar, revise sequência, fontes, riscos, pontos de controle e reversibilidade do plano proposto. Você compara o plano com seus limites antes de aprovar.
key_points: O plano é proposta sujeita a aprovação.
Fonte ou permissão ausente bloqueia o passo afetado.
moments.application: Audite o plano antes de autorizá-lo.
moments.check_question: Cada ação tem fonte e permissão?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, marque um passo a aprovar e outro a corrigir.
moments.takeaway: Aprovar o objetivo não substitui aprovar o plano.
moments.handoff: Reduza o plano a uma missão pequena e recuperável.

moments.explanation: O primeiro piloto deve ser pequeno, frequente, observável e recuperável se falhar. Neste piloto, você não envia, publica, paga nem altera sistemas externos.
key_points: Comece sem publicar, pagar ou enviar.
Teste primeiro o percurso e a evidência.
moments.application: Escolha um caso controlado e sua restauração.
moments.check_question: Você consegue voltar ao estado anterior sem depender do agente?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, defina um teste a seco e como restauraria o estado.
moments.takeaway: A primeira missão demonstra controle, não escala.
moments.handoff: Registre o piloto para decidir continuidade.

moments.explanation: O valor do piloto está na decisão informada de manter, ajustar ou aposentar seu contrato. Seu veredito decide manter, ajustar ou retirar.
key_points: Compare a evidência com a definição de concluído.
Versione mudanças e preserve exceções.
moments.application: Feche com veredito e próximo ponto de controle.
moments.check_question: Que evidência justifica continuar e qual exige parar?
moments.micro_practice: No exemplo sintético pessoal, escreva decisão, motivo, ajuste e data de revisão.
moments.takeaway: Continuidade é conquistada por evidência, não entusiasmo.
moments.handoff: Transfira o veredito ao playbook e à próxima missão.

orientation.title: Piloto pessoal, controle visível
orientation.body: Complete o workbook com uma missão individual sem efeito externo. Cada passo deixa decisão e evidência que você pode revisar. Neste piloto, toda execução ocorre fora do caderno e exige autorização separada.
orientation.use_case: Organizar notas privadas em um rascunho semanal sem enviar nem publicar.
orientation.ready_when: Você tem um caso repetível, suas fontes e tempo para revisar cada saída.

preparation_prompts.title: Filtrar o caso
preparation_prompts.purpose: Descartar casos sensíveis ou difíceis de reverter.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Liste três casos repetíveis. Avalie frequência, estabilidade, impacto da falha, observabilidade e reversibilidade. Recomende um e explique por que os outros esperam.

preparation_prompts.title: Inventariar evidência
preparation_prompts.purpose: Saber quais fontes podem ser usadas e o que falta.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Liste entradas, fontes, direitos, definição de concluído e lacunas. Marque a lacuna que exige parar ou perguntar.

preparation_prompts.title: Delimitar autoridade
preparation_prompts.purpose: Separar leitura, proposta, aprovação e ação.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Classifique cada dado, ferramenta e ação como permitido, exige aprovação ou proibido. Adicione responsável, revisor e escalonamento.

routes.title: Preparar
routes.brief: Escolher um caso reversível, fixar responsabilidade e limitar permissões.

steps.title: Escolher um caso reversível
steps.brief: Compare três processos e escolha o que permita aprender sem expor decisão sensível.
actions: Descreva entrada e resultado de cada caso.
Avalie estabilidade, impacto da falha e recuperação.
Escreva a fronteira que não delega.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: preparar rascunho semanal a partir de notas privadas.
criteria: O caso é repetível e observável.
Sua fronteira de decisão está explícita.
steps.watch_out: Escolha por controle, não por novidade.
steps.reflection: O que torna este caso adequado ao primeiro piloto?
steps.next_connection: O caso escolhido passa à definição de responsável, resultado e condição de concluído.

steps.title: Fixar responsabilidade e resultado
steps.brief: Nomeie quem decide, quem revisa e qual saída pode ser aceita.
actions: Escreva o resultado em termos observáveis.
Declare quem preserva sua aprovação final.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: você aceita ou rejeita o rascunho antes de usar.
criteria: Há uma decisão humana inequívoca.
A aprovação final permanece com você.
steps.watch_out: O agente não pode ser responsável nem aprovador.
steps.reflection: Quem responde se a saída parece correta, mas viola o contrato?
steps.next_connection: A ficha permite classificar dados, ferramentas e ações.

steps.title: Desenhar permissões e escalonamento
steps.brief: Conceda apenas a capacidade necessária e defina o que ocorre diante do limite.
actions: Marque a permissão que pode revogar.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: pode ler notas escolhidas e redigir; não pode enviar nem apagar.
criteria: Cada ação tem permissão explícita.
Você pode retirar cada permissão concedida.
steps.watch_out: Acesso técnico não é autorização.
steps.reflection: Qual permissão pode ser retirada sem perder o rascunho útil?
steps.next_connection: A matriz alimenta o briefing de missão.

routes.title: Pilotar
routes.brief: Transformar o caso em contrato, aprovar o plano e observar execução controlada.

steps.title: Redigir o briefing de missão
steps.brief: Una objetivo, contexto, fontes, restrições e definição de concluído em um contrato curto.
actions: Limite o Mission Brief a uma saída.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: produzir rascunho semanal citado a partir de notas autorizadas.
criteria: O briefing torna a saída verificável.
A saída tem definição de concluído.
steps.watch_out: Evite verbos vagos como «gerencie» ou «resolva».
steps.reflection: Qual frase poderia parecer autoridade não concedida?
steps.next_connection: O briefing vira um plano sujeito a aprovação.

steps.title: Revisar o plano antes de executar
steps.brief: Exija sequência que respeite fontes, permissões, pontos de controle e recuperação.
actions: Relacione cada passo com fonte e permissão.
Posicione aprovações e condições de parada.
Rejeite um passo fora do contrato.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: aprovar leitura e rascunho; rejeitar publicação.
criteria: Cada passo cabe no briefing.
Cada passo respeita seu contrato.
steps.watch_out: Objetivo aprovado não autoriza plano defeituoso.
steps.reflection: Qual passo deve mudar antes do teste?
steps.next_connection: Somente plano aprovado entra no caso controlado.

steps.title: Executar e registrar o piloto
steps.brief: Percorra um caso controlado e preserve evidência para reconstruir decisões e exceções.
actions: Capture entradas e versão do plano.
Registre decisões, ações propostas e pontos de controle.
Preserve o registro da execução controlada.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: guardar notas, rascunho e seu veredito; não enviar.
criteria: O registro conecta entrada, decisão e resultado.
A execução deixa registro revisável.
steps.watch_out: Saída fluida não prova conformidade.
steps.reflection: Você explicaria por que cada passo foi aceito ou rejeitado?
steps.next_connection: O registro é comparado com a definição de concluído.

routes.title: Transferir
routes.brief: Comparar evidência, decidir continuidade e revalidar antes de outro contexto.

steps.title: Comparar com a definição de concluído
steps.brief: Avalie conformidade, desvios e evidência sem premiar só aparência ou velocidade.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: o rascunho cita todas as notas, mas mistura duas datas; ajuste.
criteria: Cada veredito remete à evidência.
Seu veredito cita evidências do caso.
steps.watch_out: Não substitua critérios por impressão geral.
steps.reflection: Qual desvio muda materialmente a decisão?
steps.next_connection: Desvios passam à recuperação e correção.

steps.title: Decidir manter, ajustar ou parar
steps.brief: Feche o piloto com veredito, correções e responsabilidade.
actions: Escolha uma correção sob seu controle.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: ajustar o briefing e repetir com o mesmo escopo.
criteria: A decisão usa evidência do piloto.
A correção cabe no próximo teste.
steps.watch_out: Não amplie escopo para salvar piloto reprovado.
steps.reflection: Que evidência mudaria seu veredito?
steps.next_connection: Somente manter abre o desenho do próximo caso.

steps.title: Transferir sem ampliar por inércia
steps.brief: Reutilize o aprendizado e preserve pontos de controle até o novo contexto produzir sua própria evidência.
actions: Declare o que muda no próximo caso.
Teste o pacote sem ampliar escopo.
steps.example: Exemplo sintético: reutilizar o formato em outra pasta após revisar fontes.
criteria: Regras reutilizadas e novos pressupostos são distintos.
O novo caso preserva seus limites.
steps.watch_out: Piloto aprovado não certifica todos os casos.
steps.reflection: Qual parte do contrato perde validade ao mudar o contexto?
steps.next_connection: O pacote alimenta a próxima Masterclass ou outro piloto delimitado.

rubric.label: Incompleto
rubric.description: Faltam responsável, fontes, limites, ponto de controle ou evidência.

rubric.label: Controlado
rubric.description: O caso está delimitado e documentado, mas precisa de correção antes de repetir.

rubric.label: Transferível
rubric.description: Contrato, execução, exceções e veredito podem ser revisados e adaptados sem ampliar autoridade.

transfer_challenge.title: Desafio de transferência: uma missão, uma decisão
transfer_challenge.brief: Aplique o pacote a um novo caso e preserve o escopo até que sua própria evidência sustente a decisão.
actions: Declare o que permanece e o que muda.
Feche com manter, ajustar ou parar.
transfer_challenge.evidence: Briefing versionado, plano aprovado, registro do caso e veredito.
transfer_challenge.review_after: Revise após um caso completo; não amplie por calendário.

chapters.principle: Comece onde a falha seja visível e recuperável.
chapters.explanation: Um caso estável testa o contrato sem misturar novidade, autoridade sensível e dependência oculta.
chapters.decision: Escolha ou rejeite o caso antes de desenhar autonomia.
actions: Descarte efeitos externos e alta sensibilidade.
chapters.rule: Se não pode observar e recuperar, não é o primeiro piloto.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: rascunho de notas privadas, sem envio.
chapters.antipattern: Escolher o processo mais complexo para demonstrar ambição.
chapters.expected_evidence: Matriz de adequação e motivos de descarte.
chapters.limit: A adequação vale para o caso e escopo avaliados.

chapters.principle: A responsabilidade humana deve ser nomeável.
chapters.explanation: O agente produz ou propõe; uma pessoa responde pelo objetivo e uma revisão separada pode verificar o resultado.
chapters.decision: Atribua decisão, revisão e aceitação antes do briefing.
chapters.rule: Nenhum agente é responsável, aprovador ou fonte de autoridade.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: você aceita o rascunho e registra o motivo.
chapters.antipattern: Usar «a equipe» como responsável sem nome ou ponto de controle.
chapters.expected_evidence: Ficha de responsabilidade e vereditos.
chapters.limit: Revisão humana não corrige sozinha contrato vago.

chapters.principle: Use apenas contexto suficiente e rastreável.
chapters.explanation: Fontes autorizadas sustentam o plano; lacunas materiais são declaradas e bloqueiam o passo afetado.
chapters.decision: Autorize, limite ou exclua cada fonte.
chapters.rule: Inferência nunca substitui fonte exigida.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: usar notas selecionadas e marcar a semana ausente.
chapters.antipattern: Conceder acesso amplo «por garantia».
chapters.expected_evidence: Pacote de fontes, limites e lacunas.
chapters.limit: Mais contexto pode aumentar exposição sem melhorar relevância.

chapters.principle: Autorize capacidades separadamente e por privilégio mínimo.
chapters.explanation: Ler, classificar, redigir e agir são permissões distintas, com justificativa e revogação próprias.
chapters.decision: Conceda apenas o necessário ao rascunho verificável.
chapters.rule: O que não foi declarado permanece proibido.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: ler notas e redigir; nunca enviar ou apagar.
chapters.antipattern: Confundir acesso disponível com autoridade concedida.
chapters.expected_evidence: Matriz de permissões e registro de aprovações.
chapters.limit: Privilégio mínimo limita impacto; não elimina revisão.

chapters.principle: Toda fronteira precisa de resposta operacional.
chapters.explanation: Proibições, dados ausentes e ambiguidade levam a parar, escalar ou perguntar, nunca a improvisar autoridade.
chapters.decision: Defina qual condição ativa cada resposta.
chapters.rule: Com autoridade insuficiente, pare antes de agir.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: omitir nota não autorizada e perguntar.
chapters.antipattern: Escrever «tenha cuidado» sem conduta verificável.
chapters.expected_evidence: Tabela condição-resposta e exceções.
chapters.limit: Escalonamento não pode virar aprovação automática.

chapters.principle: Revise o plano antes de qualquer efeito.
chapters.explanation: O ponto de controle corrige sequência, fontes, permissões e reversibilidade enquanto nenhum ambiente foi alterado.
chapters.decision: Aprove, corrija ou rejeite com critérios explícitos.
actions: Emita seu veredito sobre o plano.
chapters.rule: Objetivo aprovado não autoriza todo plano.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: aprovar rascunho local; rejeitar publicação.
chapters.antipattern: Revisar somente depois que a ação ocorreu.
chapters.expected_evidence: Plano versionado e veredito do ponto de controle.
chapters.limit: Plano aprovado continua sujeito a exceção e parada.

chapters.principle: Uma execução útil pode ser reconstruída.
chapters.explanation: Entrada, versão, decisões, ações, pontos de controle, exceções e resultado formam o registro mínimo revisável.
chapters.decision: Aceite a saída somente com rastreabilidade suficiente.
actions: Registre decisões e pontos de controle.
chapters.rule: Fluidez não é evidência de conformidade.
chapters.example: Exemplo sintético: notas, rascunho, mudanças e veredito pessoal.
chapters.antipattern: Guardar apenas a saída final.
chapters.expected_evidence: Registro de execução e tabela de conformidade.
chapters.limit: O registro explica o caso; não prevê desempenho futuro.

chapters.principle: Desenhe a exceção antes que ela ocorra.
chapters.explanation: A resposta segura diz como parar, quem revisa e como descartar a saída ou restaurar o estado.
chapters.decision: Pare, escale ou recupere conforme a condição declarada.
actions: Ative responsável e ponto de controle.
